description: Spatial distribution of human population across geographic areas, typically represented as gridded data at various resolutions.
importance: Foundation for per-capita calculations (roads per 1000 people, etc.)
Essential for humanitarian planning and resource allocation
Enables population-weighted analysis of other indicators
Critical for understanding urbanization and settlement patterns

key_terms.top_down_modeling: Disaggregating census counts to grid cells using ancillary data (land cover, roads, lights)
key_terms.bottom_up_modeling: Building estimates from microcensus surveys and high-resolution imagery
key_terms.ambient_population: Average 24-hour population accounting for daytime movement (work, travel)
key_terms.constrained_estimates: Population totals adjusted to match UN national estimates
key_terms.unconstrained_estimates: Raw model outputs without adjustment to official totals

use_cases.humanitarian: Disaster response, refugee camp planning, aid distribution
use_cases.infrastructure: Roads, electricity, water access per capita
use_cases.health: Healthcare facility coverage, disease burden estimation

limitations: All gridded products are modeled estimates, not actual counts
Accuracy varies by region - typically lower in data-sparse areas
Temporal lag - census data may be 5-10 years old
